drug_class: Vitamin D analog / synthetic vitamin D
purpose: Paricalcitol is used to prevent and treat a condition called secondary hyperparathyroidism, which means your parathyroid glands are overactive. This most often happens in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who are on dialysis or have moderate to severe kidney problems. Keeping your parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels in check helps protect your bones and overall health.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally help activate vitamin D in your body, but when your kidneys aren't working well, they can't do this job properly. Paricalcitol is a man-made form of active vitamin D that steps in to do that job for your kidneys. It works by signaling your parathyroid glands to slow down and make less PTH, which helps keep calcium and phosphorus levels more balanced in your body.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or an upset stomach. You might also notice swelling, dizziness, headache, or feeling more tired than usual. Some people experience dry mouth or changes in their appetite.
warnings: Too much vitamin D can cause your calcium levels to get too high — this is called hypercalcemia. Warning signs include feeling very thirsty, urinating a lot, constipation, confusion, or muscle weakness. Tell your doctor right away if you notice these. Do not take extra calcium supplements or other vitamin D products unless your doctor says it's okay. Your doctor will regularly check your blood calcium, phosphorus, and PTH levels while you're on this medication.
typical_dosing: For people on dialysis, the dose is usually given as an injection three times a week during your dialysis sessions, or as a capsule taken by mouth. For people not on dialysis with kidney disease, it's usually taken as a capsule once or twice a day. Your doctor will start you on a low dose and adjust it based on your blood test results. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
